title: Ἐθνικά (epitome) — Ethnica; RU: Стефан Византийский, «Этника». Proposed unit: entries on Alexander's and the Diadochi's foundations
author: Stephanus of Byzantium
size: 3,655 entries in the epitome (Billerbeck count); est. 120–150k words (Meineke 1849, c. 700 pp.)
edition: Billerbeck et al., CFHB 43, 5 vols, 2006–17 (critical, with German; copyright). Meineke 1849 is public domain (Google Books; Greek on ToposText).
ru_evidence: Only excerpts: part of letter Ε translated by M. M. Kholod, Клио 2(21), 2003 (vostlit.info); Pontic and Caucasian entries in Latyshev's excerpts. No complete Russian.
en_evidence: ToposText work 241: 'a few entries … translated by Brady Kiesling'. en.wikipedia lists only Latin versions; no published English translation found.
other_translations: German: Billerbeck et al. 2006–17 (complete, with commentary). Latin: Pinedo 1678, Berkel 1688.
value: Standard reference for Greek toponyms and ethnics; nearly every entry cites an ancient authority, many of them lost (Hecataeus, Theopompus, Artemidorus, Alexander Polyhistor). Indispensable to historians, epigraphists, archaeologists. The Alexandreia entry lists 18 cities, a natural bridge to Alexander studies.
ai_feasibility: medium: formulaic Greek is easy; the risks are the grammar of ethnic forms, corrupt fragments and place identifications. Check against Billerbeck and Pleiades IDs.
pilot_unit: c. 60–80 entries on cities named after Alexander and the Diadochi (Alexandreia, Antiocheia, Seleukeia, Apameia, Laodikeia etc.), est. 8–10k words
